purpose: Model metadata for the problem-20 code-repair feedback experiment

scaffold.name: OpenCode
scaffold.test_execution: enabled via python -m pytest; tests restored and hash-checked after each run

access.notes: Key read from environment; never committed. Anthropic-compatible endpoint exists but the experiment uses the OpenAI-compatible endpoint for both consistency and tool-call stability.

pricing.peak_hours: Mon-Fri 09:00-12:00 and 14:00-18:00 Asia/Shanghai, excluding statutory holidays

experiment_cost.note: Estimate covers 24 tasks x conditions, 6-task rerun and the 8-task no-test ablation; confirm against the API bill.

risks: Vendor may roll the served version without changing the model name; pin the observed version and date in the report.
Thinking mode is on by default and adds output tokens.
Setting temperature=0 in OpenCode was observed to hang this model; do not force temperature.

access.auth: OpenCode Zen session; no separate API key
access.notes: Free-tier availability, rate limits and the exact served weights are controlled by OpenCode and are not publicly specified.

catalog_reference.source: models.dev entry opencode-go/glm-5.3-flash (different access path; not the experiment's billing)

pricing.note: The experiment uses the free tier, so actual marginal cost is $0. Do not report the catalog price as actual spend.

risks: Free tier may rate-limit or queue during peak hours; record 429/5xx rates and latency in the pilot.
The free endpoint's weights/quantization may not be identical to the paid GLM-5.3-Flash; describe it as 'GLM-5.3-Flash via OpenCode Zen free tier'.
Model ID or free-tier availability may change; freeze the exact ID and run window in the report.
evidence: local OpenCode smoke tests: read -> edit -> python -m pytest (2026-10-20)

comparability_notes: The two models differ in vendor, parameter scale, output limit and price tier; this is a comparison of two practically available low-cost code models under one scaffold, not a controlled same-scale comparison.
Both models use identical prompts, tools, permissions, step limits and test-execution mode. Only the model ID differs.
Do not generalize the result to 'vendor A is better than vendor B'; report within-model feedback effects and the between-model interaction separately.
